chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Ali ibn Ra'ab, from Durays al-Kunasi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who departed from Arafat before the setting of the sun. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Upon him is a camel (badanah) which he should sacrifice on the Day of Sacrifice. So if he is not able, he should fast for eighteen days in Makkah, or on the road, or among his family.'

key_terms.عَرَفَاتٍ: Arafat (the plain where the main rite of Hajj takes place)
key_terms.يَوْمَ النَّحْرِ: The Day of Sacrifice (10th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for leaving Arafat before sunset during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi details the fidya (expiation) for prematurely leaving Arafat before sunset, a key pillar of Hajj. It prescribes sacrificing a camel (badanah) on the Day of Nahr, with a fallback of fasting eighteen days if the pilgrim is financially unable, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on graduated penalties based on capacity. The location flexibility for fasting underscores the practical application of this ruling for pilgrims in transit or returning home.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, and Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Mahboub, from Ali Bin Raib, from Zureys Al Kunasy, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a man who departed from Arafaat before the setting of the sun. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Upon him is a camel he would sacrifice it on the Day of the Sacrifice. So if he is not able, he should Fast for eighteen days in Makkah, or in the road, or among his family’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Mahbub from ibn Ri’ab from Durays al-Kunasiy who has said the following: “I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,

about a man who leaves ‘Arafat before sunset. He (the Imam) said, ‘He owes one badanah to slaughter on the day of al-Nahr (slaughtering the offering), if unable to do this he must fast for eighteen days in Makkah or on the way or at home.’” (Fatwa best explains Hadith 4 of this Chapter)
